name: Deep Chestnut
lede: Deep Chestnut is a muted brick red, named for the chestnut.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
This swatch has more records than most descriptive names: it matches the German standard color RAL 3033, sits in the ISCC-NBS system of 1955, and is listed as a Crayola color name, per a Wikipedia list [1]. In the older Maerz and Paul dictionary its block holds the names Brazil, first recorded in 1386, and Portable Red, from 1806 [1].

The swatch is redder than the name suggests. Finlay describes an Australian painter's deep chestnut brown, made with natural pigments, which is a brown where this swatch is a red [2]. Its nearest named neighbor is [[red]], about 7 units away [1]. See also [[chestnut]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive a color near this swatch appears in 209 of 23,781 paintings, or 0.88 per cent, and it is most over-represented in India, at 3.2 times the expected rate [3]. The Kalighat painters have it in 20 of their 96 works, 4.8 times the baseline, and in a painting it is an accent 86 per cent of the time [3]. These are photographs of aged paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
